### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via generateSql (symbol, a method of class ObjectQLStrategy))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLStrategy (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via generateSql (symbol, a method of class ObjectQLStrategy))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c8cb510a5e65d25671c64061906b0954abf1fb4c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7c3cd60944a2bda37831fa13338ca360e9d017a5` — the merge of head `6c314cfe1bb6c4f2f7165509f4f57890d106449f` into base `c8cb510a5e65d25671c64061906b0954abf1fb4c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7c3cd60944a2bda37831fa13338ca360e9d017a5 && git checkout 7c3cd60944a2bda37831fa13338ca360e9d017a5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c8cb510a5e65d25671c64061906b0954abf1fb4c 6c314cfe1bb6c4f2f7165509f4f57890d106449f && git checkout -B drift-repro c8cb510a5e65d25671c64061906b0954abf1fb4c && git merge --no-ff 6c314cfe1bb6c4f2f7165509f4f57890d106449f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c8cb510a5e65d25671c64061906b0954abf1fb4c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c8cb510a5e65d25671c64061906b0954abf1fb4c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6c314cfe1bb6c4f2f7165509f4f57890d106449f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/duration-measure-sql.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/scoped-measure-key.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/cube-qualified-measure-filter.test.ts + packages/services/service-analytics/src/field-read-admission.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-executor.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/cube-registry.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/types.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/package.json, packages/runtime/src/domains/analytics.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, docs/adr/0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .changeset/25486-unknown-resource-404.md (precedent), .changeset/25906-cube-qualified-measure-filter.md (prose face, read under ②)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no `packages/spec/**` path and no governed path in the file list). Inputs read: card #25906 body and its three comments (triage 6407843769, claim 6411271126, dev report 6412534518), PR #26007 body, file list and net diff against `main` at this head, and the 52 check-runs on the head. The local checkout stands at `05f7758f`, the PR's base, and was read as the cited `main` code; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change.** On `main`, `measures: ['sales.won_amount']` on a registered dataset whose `won_amount` carries `filter: { stage: 'won' }` resolved the measure (`lookupMember` / `declaredMemberEntry` strip the own-cube qualifier) but every reader of `DatasetScope.measureFilters` indexed it by the spelling as asked, so the filter was dropped: native SQL compiled `SUM(amount)`, ObjectQL built the aggregation without `filter`, the dry-run echo rendered the unconditional form, and `namedQueryFields` (the read gate) never named `stage`. After the diff every one of those readers goes through `scopedMeasureFilter`, which resolves the name through `scopedMeasureKey`: the bare own key, else the name minus its own cube's `CUBE.` prefix, else nothing.

- **Refusal of the qualified spelling when the caller cannot read a filter field — right, and a narrowing.** `namedQueryFields` now reaches `stage` for `sales.won_amount` exactly as for `won_amount`; `assertFieldsReadable` (`callCtx`, line 1824, on both `query` and `generateSql`) hands that to `assertNamedFieldsReadable`, whose refusal is `fieldReadUnjudgeableError` / the field-read refusal in `field-read-admission.ts`: `err.code = 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` pinned against `StandardErrorCode`, `status` 403. A caller answered `200` with the unfiltered number on `main` is now refused `403`. That is a narrowing of the served set and nothing else: no new spelling is accepted, no field becomes readable, no code or status is new.
- **Correctly scoped.** (a) The bare spelling behaves identically: `scopedMeasureKey(record, 'won_amount', 'sales')` is `'won_amount'`, the same key `main` used, so nothing the bare spelling answered moves. (b) A caller who can read every field still gets `200`, now with the FILTERED number under the qualified spelling: the test's control arm (`readable: FIELDS`) runs one statement for each spelling, and the native case pins the qualified statement as byte-equal to the bare one but for the alias, with the same bound values `['won']`; the ObjectQL case pins the aggregation as `{ ...bare, alias: 'sales.won_amount' }` with `filter` present. (c) The envelope is asserted per ADR-0112: the read-gate case asserts `{ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403 }` structurally (not message sniffing), plus that the message names `stage` and that no statement ran. The REST door (`packages/runtime/src/domains/analytics.ts`, `POST /analytics/query`) calls `analyticsService.query` and lets the throw reach `resolveThrownHttpError` (`packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`), which serves a declared numeric `status` and a registered `code` as-is: the wire answer is `403` / `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the same envelope the bare spelling already got.
- **Normalisation reaches every lookup; no third lookup is left raw.** On `main` the `measureFilters?.[...]` lookups in the package's non-test source are seven: `analytics-service.ts:579` (read gate), `native-sql-strategy.ts:982` (JSON-construct routing decline), `:1127` (nested-relation routing decline), `:1351` (`compileClauses`, the statement), `objectql-strategy.ts:304` (`execute` aggregations), `:694` (`generateSql` echo), `:1055` (`filterMemberView`, the cross-object refusal). The diff rewrites all seven, and the grep of the package source at the head's base confirms there is no eighth: `dataset-executor.ts` reads `compiled.measureFilters[m]` for names it builds itself from the compiled dataset (bare by construction, `splitMeasuresByFilter`), and `preview-evaluator.ts` reads none. The `measureDurations` lookups (`:870`, `:1196`, `:1350`, `:1362`, `analytics-service.ts:555`) already went through `durationMeasureKey` / `durationMeasureIn`, which now delegate to `scopedMeasureKey`, so the two per-measure records share one rule and cannot drift. Right.
- **The two native routing declines had to move with the statement — right.** Once `compileClauses` compiles the qualified measure's filter, a `canHandle` that still indexed the filter raw would route a nested-relation or JSON-construct filter into the native compiler under the qualified spelling only. The test pins `canHandle` declining `ledger.na_count` as it declines `na_count`. One cosmetic inconsistency, not a defect: `nestedRelationConditionIn` passes `query.cube` where its siblings pass `cube.name`. They are the same string whenever a dataset scope exists: `CubeRegistry.register` keys by `cube.name`, `registerDataset` registers under `compiled.cube.name` which the compiler sets to `dataset.name`, and `getDatasetScope(query.cube)` is keyed the same way, so a cube found by `query.cube` has `cube.name === query.cube`.
- **Sibling gates on the same resolver — right, consistent, and worth naming.** `namedQueryFields` has three other consumers the diff does not touch: `queryObjects` (object-level read admission, line 1961), `assertNoInternalFieldsQueried` (`400 INVALID_FIELD` for an `internal: true` field, line 2090) and `assertStoredMetadataBodyNotQueried` (line 2238). Each now sees the qualified measure's filter fields exactly as it saw the bare spelling's. That is the same narrowing (the qualified spelling now answers what the bare one answers) through the resolver the gates and strategies share; it is correct, and it is what the card's Expected asked for. The changeset names only "the field-level read gate"; its behavioural sentence ("It answers what `measures: ['won_amount']` answers") covers the siblings exactly, so no rewrite is needed.
- **The own-cube-only prefix rule is right, not under-reaching.** `lookupMember` and `declaredMemberEntry` also resolve a measure under ANY first segment whose tail matches (`bag[tail]`, "legacy behaviour"), which raised the question whether `foreign.won_amount` reaches a strategy resolved but unfiltered. It does not: `ensureCube` (lines 3495-3497, on both `query` and `generateSql`) checks the declared key verbatim and then calls `mintableMeasureKey`, which throws `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 for every dotted spelling whose prefix is not the cube's own name (#5918 ruling). So the only dotted measure spellings that reach a strategy are own-cube qualified ones and cube-declared dotted keys (own keys). `scopedMeasureKey`'s rule mirrors that admission exactly; the test pins `other.won_amount` and a missing cube name to `undefined`, and `Object.prototype` names to `undefined` (own keys only).
- **`DatasetExecutor` / draft preview untouched — right.** The `POST /analytics/dataset/query` path and the preview branch (`analytics-service.ts:2699-2711`) hand `assertFieldsReadable` queries whose measure names come from the compiled dataset, bare, so nothing on that path changes.
- **Public surface: none.** `package.json` `exports` is `.` to `dist/index` only; `src/index.ts` does not export `scoped-measure-key.ts`, `duration-measure-sql.ts` or anything the diff touches. `durationMeasureKey` keeps its signature and semantics. No exported symbol is added, removed, renamed or re-typed.
- **Test file.** Red-first on the readers (dev report: 5 failed / 2 passed at the base with the helper present), green at the head; the ablation reverted exactly the read-gate line and exactly the read-gate case went red. The assertions are structural (`toBe` on the statement with the alias substituted, `toEqual` on params and on the aggregation object, `{ code, status }` on the refusal). Nothing in the test depends on message text beyond `toContain('stage')`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/25906-cube-qualified-measure-filter.md`: `'@objectstack/service-analytics': patch`, one package, the only package whose published source moves. Right.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on both carriers (PR body line 4, changeset line 11, each at line start, the arm as the first token in the parenthesis, as `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads it). `Metadata-protocol: none` on both. Right: nothing a metadata author writes changes, no spec key or schema moves, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` requires a declared `none` to grade every entry `patch`, which this one does.
- Repo convention for a runtime refusal of a request shape that used to run: `no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` + `patch` + BREAKING banner + ADR-0087 `not-required` (precedent `.changeset/25486-unknown-resource-404.md`, runtime/service-datasource, same five lines). The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner with FROM/NOW/FIX (Before / Now / Fix), and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the category closed on facts (no metadata moves, no export removed or narrowed, package published, no ADR-0087 id named). The `!` in the title matches the banner. `Check Changeset` is green twice on the head (08:54 and the 09:23 re-run, both `success`); `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`.
- The PR body states the departure from the claim's `Clause-②: yes (expected ...)` and why (the read gate now refuses a caller it served); the claim itself said the dev measures and declares, which is what happened. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: Clause-② measured as `no (narrowing)` against the claim's expected `yes`.** Answered: the refusal is a narrowing of the served set with nothing widened (① above); the declaration is the right one and is owed exactly this review.
- **Dev flag: the statement change is "a correction of the number, not a refusal".** Answered: a caller who could read every field and relied on the unfiltered total under the qualified name now gets the filtered number with `200`; the changeset's BREAKING banner names that number change as well as the refusal. Right.
- **Dev flag: two derived gates NOT MEASURED locally** (`check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` on a shallow clone; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needing a full build). Answered by CI on the head: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` runs the teardown-shape self-test (lint.yml:3979) and `Build Core` runs `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (ci.yml:2906); both `success` on `6c314cfe`.
- **Dev flag: dogfood battery red on one test at the base** (`test/authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts`, the `handleI18nRequest` census pin moved by #25956). Not this diff's: it touches no `packages/runtime` or `packages/qa` path; the dev filed it under `out_of_scope_findings` with dedupe words. `Dogfood Regression Gate` on the head is `success`. Escalation left to the seat: a card for the census pin, if none exists.
- **`open_questions`: []** in the dev report. None to answer.
- **Check-runs on the head: 52, all completed, none failing.** Every non-`success` conclusion is `skipped` (the opt-in harnesses, the UI matrix, Temporal conformance, Build Docs, and the first `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` rows superseded by their `success` re-runs). `Check Changeset` appeared once as `in_progress` at the first read and completed `success` at the second. `Test Core` 1-8 of 8, `TypeScript Type Check`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` job, `filter`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`: `success`.
- **Author** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay-written); the identity that produced the diff is the card thread's branch, signed below.
- **Scope held:** every path touched is under `packages/services/service-analytics/**` plus one changeset, as the claim's file surface allowed; no `packages/spec/**` path.
- **One observation, not a defect, for the seat:** the changeset's "field-level read gate" wording under-names the three sibling gates that share `namedQueryFields` (object-level read admission, the `internal: true` field gate, the stored-metadata body refusal). Its behavioural claim covers them, so no change is required.
